outcomeDiff: Match. The drift is resolved by widening config to the authoritative set; command-policy.ts and the handler are unchanged (config was the outlier). The behavior reviewer confirmed command-policy is the enforcement ceiling so REVIEW/TEST/DONE refusal is preserved and the literal additions cannot over-widen other commands.
limitations: Pure phase-policy reconciliation (2 config lines). Does NOT change dev_start behavior, the worktree bootstrap flow, or any other command's policy. The regression guard is the pre-existing assertCommandPolicyPhaseAlignment (no redundant test added).
pitfalls: The drift had THREE sources to reconcile against: the dev_start handler's own allowedPhases guard (worktree.ts:823, which REQUIRES INIT because the atomic story_advance INIT_CHECK flow calls dev_start while the story is still at INIT), command-policy.ts:130, and config.ts DEFAULT_PHASE_TOOLS — the first two agreed on the 4-phase set, config was the outlier, so the correct direction was to widen config (narrowing command-policy would have contradicted the handler and removed the documented DEV recovery path). isCommandAllowed (consuming DEFAULT_PHASE_TOOLS) is a real runtime gate but sits UNDER the command-policy ceiling, so widening config could not over-widen beyond REVIEW/TEST/DONE refusal.
